speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the 32.6% increase in scam cases and 13 scam syndicates busted in 2022 (a) whether more resources will be deployed by the Ministry and relevant agencies in the financial sector to deal with the growing case load; and (b) whether more can be done in collaboration with other law enforcement agencies in other jurisdictions to track and arrest culprits responsible for the scam cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police also partner stakeholders from the public and private sectors in our fight against scams, to complement and supplement our own capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They worked with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) to co-locate staff from six major banks at the Anti-Scam Command.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Staff from the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) are also co-located at the Anti-Scam Command to support Police investigations in Singpass-related scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This has enhanced the Police's capabilities to more expeditiously stop more people from falling prey to ongoing scams and freeze bank accounts before the scammed monies flow out of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MAS also works closely with the Standing Committee on Fraud of the ABS to drive anti-scam efforts in the financial industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This includes implementing robust measures to safeguard customers, such as putting in place an emergency "kill switch" for customers to swiftly freeze their bank accounts which they suspect may have been compromised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police have leveraged technology to enhance our ability to deal with scams and facilitate quicker decision-making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For instance, they use analytics to detect and block scam websites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This includes tools that look out for tell-tale characteristics of scam websites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As scammers are mostly based overseas, our efforts to solve scam cases depend significantly on the cooperation from foreign law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We are keen to enhance collaboration with foreign law enforcement agencies, but this will depend on their capacity and receptivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Where possible, the Police work with overseas counterparts to exchange information and conduct joint operations to dismantle scam syndicates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since 2017, the Police have been a member of the multilateral platform called the Asset-Recovery Interagency Network – Asia Pacific.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The network spans 28 member jurisdictions within the Asia-Pacific region and aims to increase the effectiveness of members' efforts in depriving criminals of their illicit profits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: INTERPOL also plays a crucial role in our fight against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They provide a platform for the Police to collaborate and share intelligence with the larger international policing community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2022, the Police participated in Operation HAECHI III, a global operation coordinated by INTERPOL over five months to tackle cyber-enabled financial crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have also put in place upstream measures to try to prevent scammers from approaching Singaporeans in the first place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such measures include working with telcos to block SMSes sent from unregistered sender IDs and overseas calls attempting to spoof domestic phone numbers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Ultimately, the best defence against scams is a discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A for ADD(ing) security features, such as installing the ScamShield app; C for CHECK(ing) for scam signs and to verify with official sources; and T for TELL(ing) authorities, family and friends about scams.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I certainly agree with the importance of education.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I have been also very supportive on-the-ground, for all the education efforts.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Are we prepared to trade off speed and convenience of transactions to protect our users, at least, until we see a drop in scam cases?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: And I was also told that seniors are now stopped being given the PayNow facility by banks.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: But the question is, instead of excluding our seniors from tools like PayNow, for large transaction amounts, are we able to get the banks and financial institutions to look at how they can differentiate, say, new PayNow numbers from the usual list, so that the banks can have enough time to pre-screen the numbers before these big amounts of transactions are allowed?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, we need to balance having an efficient and effective banking system, versus having security features in place to protect our customers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This particular point about the introduction of a cooling period is an important point, especially when it involves seniors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They may, unfortunately, sometimes be conned, scammed into setting up an Internet banking facility.
